t2.descripcion:
In the 19th century, Spain experiences Romanticism (first half) and Realism (second half). Romanticism exalts freedom, feeling and imagination; Bécquer stands out with his Rimas and Leyendas, and Espronceda with his rebellious poetry. In romantic theater, the historical drama of Duque de Rivas and Zorrilla. Realism portrays contemporary society with objectivity; Pérez Galdós with the Episodios Nacionales and Fortunata y Jacinta, Clarín with La Regenta, and Pardo Bazán with Los Pazos de Ulloa. In art, Romanticism is reflected in Goya (although straddling two centuries) and Realism in genre painting.
• Romanticism defends individual freedom.
• Bécquer is the most widely read romantic poet.
• Realism describes everyday life in detail.
• Galdós and Clarín are the great realist novelists.
• La Regenta is a critique of provincial society.

📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: Spanish Romanticism is later than European Romanticism and is marked by the return of exiles. Realism emerges as a reaction to romantic idealism.

❌ COMMON ERROR: Chinese students often confuse 'romanticism' with 'romance novel'; in literature, Romanticism is a rebellious and melancholic movement. They also believe that Goya is only a romantic painter, but his work spans from rococo to premodern expressionism.
ejemplos: Bécquer escribió las 'Rimas' y 'Leyendas'.
La Regenta de Clarín critica la hipocresía social.
Galdós retrata la sociedad madrileña del siglo XIX.
El Romanticismo exalta el 'yo' y la naturaleza.
El Realismo usa un narrador omnisciente.

t4.titulo: Latin American Literature: From Modernism to the Boom
t4.descripcion:
Latin American literature has had a global impact. Modernism, led by Rubén Darío, renews poetry in Spanish. In the 20th century, Jorge Luis Borges (fantastic short stories), Pablo Neruda (love and political poetry), Gabriel García Márquez (Cien años de soledad, magical realism), Julio Cortázar (Rayuela), Mario Vargas Llosa and Carlos Fuentes stand out. The 'boom' of the 60s and 70s projects this literature internationally. In art, Mexican muralism (Rivera, Orozco, Siqueiros) and the architecture of Barragán are important contributions.
• Modernism renews poetic language.
• Borges plays with metafiction and eternity.
• García Márquez is the Nobel laureate of magical realism.
• Cortázar innovates with 'Rayuela' and its open structure.
• Mexican muralism has a strong social commitment.

📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: The term 'boom' refers to a publishing phenomenon, not a homogeneous movement. Many boom authors lived in Europe and were influenced by the avant-garde.

❌ COMMON MISTAKE: Chinese students often reduce Latin American literature to magical realism, but there is much variety: poetry, essay, fantastic short story. They also confuse Borges with a novelist, when he is mainly a short story writer and essayist.
ejemplos: Rubén Darío inició el modernismo con 'Azul'.
García Márquez ganó el Nobel en 1982.
Borges escribió 'El Aleph' y 'Ficciones'.
Cortázar propone una lectura activa en 'Rayuela'.
Rivera pintó murales sobre la historia de México.

t1.titulo: The Golden Age: literature and art
t1.descripcion:
The Golden Age (16th and 17th centuries) is the period of maximum splendor of letters and arts in Spain. In literature, the mystical poetry of San Juan de la Cruz and Santa Teresa, the narrative of Cervantes with the Quijote, and the theater of Lope de Vega and Calderón stand out. In art, the Baroque is manifested in the painting of Velázquez and Zurbarán, and in Herrerian architecture.
• The picaresque novel reflects marginalized society.
• Baroque theater mixes the comic and the tragic.
• The culteran poetry of Góngora and the conceptist poetry of Quevedo.
• The Quijote parodies chivalric novels.
• The Baroque is characterized by contrast and movement.

📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: The Golden Age spans more than a century and is not limited to a single generation. It is essential to contextualize the works in their historical framework (Reconquista, Empire, Counter-Reformation).

❌ COMMON ERROR: Chinese students often translate 'Siglo de Oro' as a generic 'golden age', but in Spanish it refers specifically to this cultural period. They also confuse Góngora and Quevedo; remember that Góngora is more obscure and culterano, while Quevedo is more satirical and conceptista.
ejemplos: El Quijote es la obra cumbre de la literatura española.
Lope de Vega escribió cientos de comedias.
Velázquez pintó 'Las Meninas' en el siglo XVII.
Góngora y Quevedo fueron rivales literarios.
El Barroco se caracteriza por el claroscuro.

t3.titulo: The avant-garde movements and the Generation of '27
t3.descripcion:
At the beginning of the 20th century, the European avant-garde movements (futurism, cubism, surrealism) arrive in Spain. In literature, the Generation of '27 (Lorca, Alberti, Cernuda, Salinas, Guillén, Aleixandre, etc.) combines tradition and avant-garde. Lorca stands out for his poetry and theatre (Bodas de sangre, La casa de Bernarda Alba). In art, Picasso, Dalí and Miró are key figures of surrealism and cubism. The Civil War (1936-1939) marks a before and after; many artists go into exile.
• The Generation of '27 mixes the popular and the learned.
• Lorca is the most universal poet and playwright.
• Surrealism influences Dalí and Buñuel.
• Picasso revolutionises painting with cubism.
• Republican exile enriches the culture of other countries.

📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: The Generation of '27 is not a homogeneous group; its members have diverse styles, but they share the tribute to Góngora in 1927. Spanish surrealism has a very personal character.

❌ COMMON MISTAKE: Chinese students often think that all artists of the period are surrealists; in reality, there is a mixture of movements. They also confuse Lorca with a merely rural poet, when his work is very varied and cosmopolitan.
ejemplos: Lorca wrote 'Bodas de sangre' in 1933.
Dalí and Buñuel collaborated on 'Un perro andaluz'.
The Generation of '27 paid tribute to Góngora.
Picasso painted 'Guernica' in 1937.
Surrealism seeks to liberate the unconscious.

dict.西班牙语文学是时代与风格的马赛克。在黄金时代，塞万提斯通过《堂吉诃德》创作了一部: Spanish literature is a mosaic of eras and styles. In the Golden Age, Cervantes created a work that revolutionized the novel with Don Quixote, while poets such as Góngora and Quevedo explored the Baroque style with complex metaphors. Romanticism in the 19th century brought an exaltation of the self and freedom, and the introspective poetry of writers like Bécquer still moves us today. Later, Realism portrayed society with precision, as Galdós did in his novels.
dict.世纪，先锋派打破常规，27一代将传统与实验结合；例如，洛尔迦为戏剧和诗歌赋予了声: In the 20th century, the avant-garde broke conventions, and the Generation of '27 combined tradition with experimentation; for example, Lorca gave voice to theater and poetry. Across the Atlantic, Rubén Darío's modernism renewed verse, and the Latin American boom brought narrative to readers worldwide, with writers such as García Márquez. Spanish literature, marked by exile and social criticism, remains alive and constantly reinvents itself.

dict.马德里的普拉多博物馆不仅收藏了委拉斯开兹和戈雅的画作，还反映了艺术与文学之间的关: The Prado Museum in Madrid not only houses paintings by Velázquez and Goya but also reflects the relationship between art and literature. Many Golden Age paintings depict mythological and religious scenes that inspired writers. For example, Velázquez's Las Meninas has been the subject of literary and philosophical analysis. In addition, the Prado hosts exhibitions that connect works of art with literary texts, showing how painting and literature have dialogued throughout history.
dict.在中国，故宫博物院也收藏了许多与文学相关的艺术品，如书法和绘画，体现了“诗画一体: In China, the Palace Museum also houses many literary-related artworks, such as calligraphy and painting, embodying the tradition of 'poetry and painting as one.' Both show the close connection between art and literature.

For /r/, the tip of the tongue taps quickly once or several times, while for /l/, the tip of the tongue touches the upper alveolar ridge and air flows out through the sides. Practice words like 'arte' and 'alte' (which doesn't exist, but is used for contrast) to feel the difference.
